# Asterisk Configuration

- Version: **Asterisk 22.5.2** (Debian/Ubuntu package), config dir `/etc/asterisk`, runs as `asterisk`.
- `deploy/setup.sh` was run in **integrate** mode (the default): the stock Debian config is kept and only a few lines
  were added. The lightweight templates in `deploy/asterisk/` are only used in `ASTERISK_MODE=full` and are **not**
  what is live.
- Every run of setup.sh makes a backup: `/etc/asterisk/backup-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS/` (11 backups from 2026-10-06 exist).

## Files and who owns them

### Generated by the app — never edit by hand

| File | Written by | Content | Reloaded with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/etc/asterisk/sipdist/trunks.conf` | `renderTrunks()` | per active trunk: `[t_<name>]` aor, `[t_<name>-auth]` (if user/pass), `[t_<name>]` endpoint, `[t_<name>-identify]`, `[t_<name>-reg]` (if register) | `res_pjsip.so`, `res_pjsip_outbound_registration.so` |
| `/etc/asterisk/sipdist/processes.conf` | `renderProcesses()` | per process: `[p_<code>]` aor (first fixed IP), endpoint, `[p_<code>-identify]` with `match=` per allowed IP (password auth: `-auth` section, plus `deny`/`permit` on the endpoint if IPs are set). Active IP processes also get a monitor-only `[p_<code>-mon]` AOR + endpoint: `qualify_frequency=60` OPTIONS ping to each fixed IP for the Processes page Connection column. It is separate from `[p_<code>]` because Asterisk skips `Unavail` contacts when dialing, so a customer that ignores OPTIONS still gets inbound calls; it is never identified (`identify_by=ip`, no identify section; a request naming it gets 401) and its context `sd-none` does not exist | `res_pjsip.so` |
| `/etc/asterisk/sipdist/dialplan.conf` | `renderDialplan()` | `[sd-hangup]`, `[sd-inhdr]`, `[sd-from-trunk]`, `[proc-<code>]`, `[sd-cli-<trunk>]`, `[sd-didok-<trunk>]`, `[sd-in-<trunk>]` | `pbx_config.so` |

Directory: owner `asterisk:asterisk`, mode `2750`; files mode `0640`. The systemd unit allows writes only to this
directory (`ProtectSystem=full`, `ReadWritePaths=/etc/asterisk/sipdist`).
Preview without writing: UI → System → config preview, or `npm run render`.

### Edited by setup.sh (integrate mode) — live server

| File | Change made | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `/etc/asterisk/pjsip.conf` (end of file, ~line 1764) | `[transport-udp]` and `[transport-tcp]` on `0.0.0.0:5060` (flat LAN, no NAT lines); `#tryinclude sipdist/trunks.conf`; `#tryinclude sipdist/processes.conf`; `[global] endpoint_identifier_order=ip,auth_username,username,anonymous` | load generated endpoints; identify customers/carriers by IP first |
| `/etc/asterisk/extensions.conf` (line ~916) | `#tryinclude sipdist/dialplan.conf` | load generated contexts |
| `/etc/asterisk/modules.conf` | ensures needed modules are not `noload` (stock file has `autoload=yes`) | `res_pjsip_endpoint_identifier_ip`, `app_userevent`, `func_groupcount`, `res_ari*`, … |
| `/etc/asterisk/ari.conf` (line ~76) | user `[sipdist]`, `type=user`, `read_only=no`, `password_format=plain`, `password=…` | Node backend ARI login — must match `ARI_USER`/`ARI_PASS` in `.env` |
| `/etc/asterisk/http.conf` | `enabled=yes`, `bindaddr=127.0.0.1`, `bindport=8088` | ARI on loopback only |

| `/etc/asterisk/asterisk.conf` `[options]` | `maxfiles = 1048576` (by hand, 2026-10-08) | open file handles for many concurrent calls — see [operations.md § Capacity](operations.md#capacity-and-tuning) |
| `/etc/asterisk/rtp.conf` | `rtpend=30000` (by hand, 2026-10-08; was the stock 20000) | RTP ports **10000–30000** = 10,000 media streams ≈ 5,000 calls |
| `/etc/systemd/system/asterisk.service.d/sipdist-limits.conf` | `LimitNOFILE=1048576`, `LimitNPROC=infinity`, `TasksMax=infinity` (from `deploy/asterisk-limits.conf`, installed by setup.sh) | the systemd default soft limit of 1024 files capped Asterisk at ~200 calls |

Backup of the files before the 2026-10-08 change: `/etc/asterisk/backup-limits-20261008-091031/`.

Not configured live: `cdr_pgsql.conf` (stock file; `cdr_pgsql.so` not running).

### Templates in the repo (`deploy/asterisk/`, full mode only)

`asterisk.conf`, `modules.conf` (`autoload=no`, only PJSIP/ARI/dialplan modules), `pjsip.conf`, `extensions.conf`,
`ari.conf`, `http.conf`, `cdr.conf`, `cdr_pgsql.conf`, `logger.conf`, `rtp.conf`. Placeholders `__EXTERNAL_IP__`,
`__ARI_USER__`, `__ARI_PASS__`, `__DB_HOST__`, `__DB_PORT__`, `__DB_NAME__`, `__DB_USER__`, `__DB_PASS__` are replaced
by setup.sh with `sed`.

## Naming conventions

| Object | Asterisk name |
|---|---|
| Trunk `<name>` | endpoint/aor `t_<name>`, auth `t_<name>-auth`, identify `t_<name>-identify`, registration `t_<name>-reg` |
| Process `<code>` | endpoint/aor `p_<code>`, identify `p_<code>-identify`, auth `p_<code>-auth`, context `proc-<code>`, monitor-only endpoint/aor `p_<code>-mon` (IP auth, OPTIONS ping) |
| Channel names | `PJSIP/p_<code>-xxxxxxxx`, `PJSIP/t_<name>-xxxxxxxx` (tracker counts by this pattern) |
| Groups | `<code>@sdproc` (process limit), `<name>@sdtrunk` (trunk limit) — `asterisk -rx "group show channels"` |

## Endpoint settings rendered

Trunks: `context=sd-in-<name>` if inbound allowed and DID ranges exist, else `sd-from-trunk`; `direct_media=no`,
`rtp_symmetric=yes`, `force_rport=yes`, `rewrite_contact=yes`, `send_rpid=yes`, `trust_id_outbound=yes`, `timers=no`,
`qualify_frequency=60`. Registration: retry 30 s, forbidden/fatal retry 300 s, expiration 3600, `line=yes`.

Processes: `context=proc-<code>`, `identify_by=ip`, `trust_id_inbound=yes`, `allow_subscribe=no`, AOR
`contact=sip:<first fixed IP>:<sip_port>` (used for inbound calls to the customer; `sip_port` per process, default 5060).

Optional env `PJSIP_TRANSPORT_UDP` / `PJSIP_TRANSPORT_TCP` adds `transport=<name>` lines; not set live (PJSIP picks the
matching transport).

## Dialplan contexts (generated)

| Context | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `[sd-hangup]` | Hangup handler on every SIPDist channel. Fills `SD_DISP` from `DIALSTATUS` if empty, sends `UserEvent(SIPDIST_END, proc, trunk, num, out, cli, cliout, disp, dialstatus, cause, start, end, bill, dialed, uid, linked, src, dir, did, hst, hdid, hnum)` |
| `[sd-inhdr]` | Pre-dial subroutine on inbound legs: adds `X-DID` / `X-Number` headers |
| `[sd-from-trunk]` | Rejects carrier calls (cause 21) on trunks without inbound |
| `[proc-<code>]` | Outbound: dummy number → header checks → hours → limits → Dial trunk. Any other number → INVALID |
| `[sd-didok-<trunk>]` | Sets `SD_DIDOK=1` if `SD_DID` is inside a caller-ID range |
| `[sd-cli-<trunk>]` | Picks a random caller-ID DID (weighted by range size) — generated but not used by the current header-only flow |
| `[sd-in-<trunk>]` | Inbound DID routing (see [architecture.md](architecture.md#inbound-call-flow-carrier--customer)) |

Every process context starts with `exten => h,1,Hangup()` so the `_.` catch-all does not run at hangup and overwrite
`SD_DISP`.

Channel variables used: `SD_START, SD_PROC, SD_TRUNK, SD_NUM, SD_CLI, SD_SRC, SD_DISP, SD_OUT, SD_CLIOUT, SD_DIR,
SD_DID, SD_DIDUSED, SD_DIDOK, SD_HST, SD_HDID, SD_HNUM, SD_CNUM, SD_DEST, SD_INPROC, SD_ASG, SD_CUST, SD_DIDM`.

## Modules required

`res_pjsip`, `chan_pjsip`, `res_pjsip_endpoint_identifier_ip`, `res_pjsip_endpoint_identifier_user`,
`res_pjsip_outbound_registration`, `res_pjsip_header_funcs` (PJSIP_HEADER), `pbx_config`, `app_dial`,
`app_userevent`, `func_groupcount`, `func_channel`, `func_callerid`, `func_logic`, `func_strings`, `func_curl` +
`res_curl` (inbound routing CURL), `res_http_websocket`, `res_stasis`, `res_ari`, `res_ari_channels`,
`res_ari_events`, `res_ari_asterisk`, `res_ari_endpoints`. All are running on the live server.

## Customer-side configuration

The UI (Processes → peer config, `GET /api/processes/:id/peer-config`) generates a ready PJSIP and chan_sip/ViciDial
sample for the customer: an endpoint `sipdist` pointing at `PUBLIC_IP:SIP_PORT`, and a dialplan that dials the
dummy number with headers `X-DID: <caller-ID DID>` and `X-Number: <customer number>`. Inbound calls arrive at the
customer in context `from-sipdist` (number = caller, caller ID = DID). Password-auth processes also get a registration
(`[sipdist-reg] type=registration`, chan_sip `register =>`), always — it makes them show online and receive inbound
DID calls / callbacks. IP-auth processes get none.

## Useful Asterisk commands

```bash
asterisk -rx 'pjsip show endpoints'          # p_* and t_* endpoints and state
asterisk -rx 'pjsip show registrations'      # t_*-reg
asterisk -rx 'pjsip show contacts'
asterisk -rx 'group show channels'           # live limit counters
asterisk -rx 'core show channels concise'
asterisk -rx 'dialplan show proc-<code>'
asterisk -rx 'pjsip set logger on'           # SIP trace (turn off afterwards)
asterisk -rx 'ari show users'
asterisk -rx 'module reload res_pjsip.so'    # same as the app does
```
